# What is inside an R installation {.dark-slide background-color="#111C26"}

[BLOCK 1 &middot; PART B]{.eyebrow}

::: {.accent-bar}
:::

## Where is R?

::: {.demo-label}
Live
:::

```bash
which R
```

```text
/usr/bin/R
``` 

or better:

```bash
which -a R Rscript
```

```text
/usr/bin/R
/bin/R
/usr/bin/Rscript
/bin/Rscript
```

On a server with several R versions, the first hit is not necessarily the
one you want. `which -a` lists all of them.

## `R` is a shell script

```bash
head -6 "$(which R)"
```

```text
#!/bin/bash
# Shell wrapper for R executable.

R_HOME_DIR="/usr/lib/R"
if test "${R_HOME_DIR}" = "/usr/lib/R"; then
   case "linux-gnu" in
```

The path to the installation is **hard-coded into the script at build time**.
This is exactly why you cannot move an R installation by copying the
directory, and why `--prefix` matters at `configure` time.

R also reports the installation path itself:

```shell
R RHOME
```

```text
/usr/lib/R
```

R-admin calls this path `R_HOME` ([R-admin](https://cran.r-project.org/doc/manuals/r-release/R-admin.html)).

## What the script does before it execs

The script ends by `exec`ing another program:

```bash
grep -n 'exec' "$(which R)" | tail -5
```

```text
144:      exec sh "${R_HOME}/bin/Rcmd" "${@}" ;;
252:R_binary="${R_HOME}/bin/exec${R_ARCH}/R"
273:  exec "${R_binary}"  ${args} "${@}"
298:    exec ${debugger} ${debugger_args} "${R_binary}"
300:    exec ${debugger} ${debugger_args} "${R_binary}" ${args} "${@}"
```

Along the way it:

- sets `R_HOME`, `R_SHARE_DIR`, `R_INCLUDE_DIR`, `R_DOC_DIR`
- sources `${R_HOME}/etc/ldpaths` to fix up `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`
- dispatches `R CMD ...`, `R --version`, `R RHOME` without starting R at all
- finally execs the real binary

## Trying it out 

The real executable is under `bin/exec/`.

::: {.demo-label}
Live
:::

```bash
head -c 4 /usr/lib/R/bin/exec/R | od -c | head -1
```

```text
0000000 177   E   L   F
```


```bash
/usr/lib/R/bin/exec/R --vanilla -q -e '1+1'
```

```text
Fatal error: R home directory is not defined
```

## And fixing it

```bash
R_HOME=/usr/lib/R /usr/lib/R/bin/exec/R --vanilla -q -e 'R.version.string'
```

```text
> R.version.string
[1] "R version 4.6.1 (2026-06-24)"
```

::: {.note}
[Why this matters]{.note-label}
A service or tool that runs `bin/exec/R` directly, instead of the `R`
script, skips both jobs of the wrapper: setting `R_HOME` and sourcing
`etc/ldpaths` for `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`
([R.sh.in](https://github.com/wch/r-source/blob/trunk/src/scripts/R.sh.in)).
On this image `R_HOME` is enough.
:::

## `R_HOME` directory structure

```bash
R RHOME
ls "$(R RHOME)"
```

```text
bin  COPYING  etc  lib  library  modules  site-library  SVN-REVISION
```

| Directory | Contents |
|---|---|
| `bin/` | The `R` and `Rscript` wrappers, `exec/R`, and the `R CMD` helper scripts |
| `etc/` | `Renviron`, `Renviron.site`, `Rprofile.site`, `Makeconf`, `ldpaths` |
| `library/` | `.Library`: base and recommended packages |
| `site-library/` | `.Library.site`, if it exists: where you put site packages |
| `lib/` | `libR.so` and friends |
| `modules/` | Loadable modules: `lapack.so`, `internet.so`, `R_X11.so` |

A source build also has `share/` and `doc/` here. Debian relocates those to
`/usr/share/R/` and `/usr/share/doc/r-base-core/`. One more reason to ask
`R RHOME` rather than assume a layout.

## On Debian, `etc/` is somewhere else

```bash
ls -l "$(R RHOME)/etc"
```

```text
-rw-r--r-- 1 root root  234 javaconf
lrwxrwxrwx 1 root root   14 ldpaths       -> /etc/R/ldpaths
lrwxrwxrwx 1 root root   15 Makeconf      -> /etc/R/Makeconf
lrwxrwxrwx 1 root root   15 Renviron      -> /etc/R/Renviron
lrwxrwxrwx 1 root root   20 Renviron.site -> /etc/R/Renviron.site
-rw-r--r-- 1 root root 2210 Renviron.ucf
lrwxrwxrwx 1 root root   19 repositories  -> /etc/R/repositories
lrwxrwxrwx 1 root root   20 Rprofile.site -> /etc/R/Rprofile.site
```

Debian and Ubuntu symlink the configuration into `/etc/R/` so that it
survives package upgrades and belongs to the sysadmin rather than the
package manager. A source build has real files in `$(R RHOME)/etc`.

Either way, **`$(R RHOME)/etc` is R's default site-wide configuration location**. 

`repositories` is Debian's own addition: the menu `chooseCRANmirror()` offers.
`Renviron.ucf` is the packaging system's reference copy, used to detect
whether you have edited `Renviron` (do not edit it).

## `R` versus `Rscript`

::: {.demo-label}
Live
:::

```bash
head -1 "$(which R)"
```

```text
#!/bin/bash
```

```bash
head -c 4 "$(which Rscript)" | od -c | head -1
```

```text
0000000 177   E   L   F
```

**`R` is a shell script. `Rscript` is a compiled binary.**

## `Rscript` runs the `R` script

```bash
Rscript --verbose -e '1+1'
```

```text
running
  '/usr/lib/R/bin/R --no-echo --no-restore -e 1+1'

[1] 2
```

`Rscript` is a small binary with R's install path compiled into it (an
`RHOME` environment variable overrides it). It runs the `R` shell script from
there
([Rscript.c](https://github.com/wch/r-source/blob/trunk/src/unix/Rscript.c)).

```text
R        ->  bin/R (script)  ->  bin/exec/R
Rscript  ->  bin/R (script)  ->  bin/exec/R
```

Both end up in the wrapper, so both set `R_HOME` themselves. Only running
`bin/exec/R` directly needs `R_HOME` from outside.

## The behavioural differences

| | `R` | `Rscript` |
|---|---|---|
| Form | `#!/bin/bash` wrapper, ~300 lines | ELF binary, ~15 KB |
| Echoes input | Yes | No (`--no-echo` implied) |
| `--no-save` | Implied by `-e`, otherwise must be given | Implied |
| `--no-restore` | Must be given | Implied |
| Startup files | Read | Read, **the same ones** |
| Default packages | `R_DEFAULT_PACKAGES` | `R_SCRIPT_DEFAULT_PACKAGES` first, else `R_DEFAULT_PACKAGES` |

`-e` implies `--no-save` unless `--save` is given
([R-intro](https://cran.r-project.org/doc/manuals/r-release/R-intro.html#Invoking-R-from-the-command-line)).

```bash
R -q -e 'cat("hi\n")'
```

```text
> cat("hi\n")
hi
>
```

```bash
Rscript -e 'cat("hi\n")'
```

```text
hi
```

## Two things that are *not* different

::: {.demo-label}
Live
:::

```bash
R -q --no-echo --no-restore -e 'cat(length(search()), interactive(), "\n")'
Rscript                   -e 'cat(length(search()), interactive(), "\n")'
```

```text
9 FALSE
9 FALSE
```

**Default packages are the same.** Both attach the same nine environments
unless you set `R_SCRIPT_DEFAULT_PACKAGES`.

**Neither is interactive.** `interactive()` is `FALSE` for `R -e` too. Code
that branches on `interactive()` to decide whether to prompt will not prompt
under either.

::: {.note}
[Attach only `base`]{.note-label}
`R_SCRIPT_DEFAULT_PACKAGES=NULL` makes `Rscript` attach only `base`, and
takes precedence over `R_DEFAULT_PACKAGES`
([`?Rscript`](https://stat.ethz.ch/R-manual/R-devel/library/utils/html/Rscript.html),
[`?Startup`](https://stat.ethz.ch/R-manual/R-devel/library/base/html/Startup.html)).
:::

## `Rscript` reads the same startup files

```bash
Rscript          -e 'getOption("repos")'
Rscript --vanilla -e 'getOption("repos")'
```

`Rscript` reads the same startup files as `R`. `--vanilla` skips the site
and user files: `Renviron.site`, `Rprofile.site`, `.Renviron` and
`.Rprofile`. `$(R RHOME)/etc/Renviron` is still read
([`?Startup`](https://stat.ethz.ch/R-manual/R-devel/library/base/html/Startup.html)).

::: {.note}
[Rule]{.note-label}
`--vanilla` skips `Rprofile.site`, so a job run as `Rscript --vanilla job.R`
does not see the repository or library you configured there. Put what the
job needs in the script (`repos =`, `lib =`) or, for settings R reads from
environment variables such as `R_LIBS_SITE`, in the job's environment.
:::

## `Rscript` in a `#!` line

`Rscript` is meant for executable scripts
([`?Rscript`](https://stat.ethz.ch/R-manual/R-devel/library/utils/html/Rscript.html)):

```r
#!/usr/bin/Rscript --vanilla
args <- commandArgs(trailingOnly = TRUE)
cat("Hello,", args[1], "\n")
```

```bash
chmod +x hello.R
./hello.R world
```

```text
Hello, world
```

- Options on the `#!` line go to `Rscript`; arguments to the script end up
  in `commandArgs(trailingOnly = TRUE)`.
- `#!/usr/bin/env Rscript` takes the first `Rscript` on `PATH`. With an
  option, use `#!/usr/bin/env -S Rscript --vanilla`
  ([GNU env](https://www.gnu.org/software/coreutils/manual/html_node/env-invocation.html#g_t_002dS_002f_002d_002dsplit_002dstring-usage-in-scripts)).

## `R --help` and important flags

::: {.demo-label}
Live
:::

```bash
R --help
```

| Flag | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--vanilla` | `--no-save --no-restore --no-site-file --no-init-file --no-environ` |
| `--no-init-file` | Skip the user profile (`./.Rprofile` or `~/.Rprofile`) |
| `--no-site-file` | Skip `Rprofile.site` |
| `--no-environ` | Skip `.Renviron` and `Renviron.site` |
| `-e <expr>` | Run an expression; repeatable |
| `-q` | Do not print the startup banner |
| `--no-echo` | Do not echo input |
| `--max-connections=N` | Raise R's limit on open connections (files, URLs, sockets; default 128, max 4096; [`?connections`](https://stat.ethz.ch/R-manual/R-devel/library/base/html/connections.html)) |

If a problem disappears under `R --vanilla`, it comes from a site or user
startup file, or from a saved `.RData`.

## `R CMD` administrator and developer tools

`R CMD` runs tools that ship with R, with `R_HOME` and the toolchain
already set up correctly. We use four of these today.

```bash
R CMD --help
```

| Command | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `R CMD INSTALL` | Install a package from source or tarball into a library |
| `R CMD build` | Turn a source *directory* into a `.tar.gz` |
| `R CMD check` | Run the full quality check suite on a tarball |
| `R CMD config` | Report the build's compilers and flags |
| `R CMD Rd2pdf`, `Sweave`, `Rprof` | The rest of the toolbox |

Each command has its own help:

```bash
R CMD INSTALL --help
```
